thread:
Alex: uploaded an nsys capture for the 3pm regression run, looks like weird hostcopy/kernels overlap. link: https://internal-artifacts/trace/2629.nsys
Priya: thanks — quick summary? what did the timeline show at a glance?
Alex: kernels were executing while host-to-device memcpy started, but memcpy seems to serialize across streams in the middle of long kernels. nsight shows copy engine toggling, then a long CPU gap where the app thread is asleep.
Jamie: do we have the nsys command used? want to reproduce locally
Alex: ran `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,cudnn --sample=none -o trace_2629 ./bench_runner --batch=1 --seq=1024`
Marco: hmm batch=1 + high seq len can expose KV cache prefetching + lots of small H2D uploads. Could be pinnedpool exhaustion forcing sync copies.
Sasha: I see two candidate causes -- (1) GPU copy engine saturated and driver serializes host copies when pinned buffer allocation misses, (2) CPU scheduler preempted the thread that submits async copies, so copies appear serialized from trace.
Alex: timeline snippet (textified):
```
GPU0: [kernel K1: 0-12ms] [kernel K2: 13-25ms]
H2D : [copy C1: 5-7ms] [copy C2: 14-16ms] <-- gaps aligning with CPU sleep
CPU : submit thread awake 0-6ms, sleeps 6-11ms, awake 11-26ms
```
Priya: that sleep window lines up with a syslog spike? check dmesg or perf samples for CPU steal
Marco: I checked perf top on the host, saw frequent glibc epoll_wait in the submitter during the lull. Might be batching heuristic waiting for more tok/requests then fallback to synchronous flush.
Jamie: can you paste NVTX annotations? maybe batcher emitted a flush marker
Alex: yes NVTX shows `batcher/flush` at 6ms and 14ms. The runtime's heuristic tries to wait 4ms for coalescing, then force-flush when seq/timeout hit.
Sasha: plausible root: the batcher heuristic causes submit thread to sleep (timed wait), then on wake we allocate pinned buffer for the copy. If pinned pool was exhausted driver falls back to pageable copy which serializes and blocks CPU until copy completes.
Alex: reproduced locally with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=0 PYTHONHASHSEED=0 ./bench_runner` and a small pinned pool size — see pinnedpool.log attached (uploaded).
infra-bot: pinned pool low watermark detected for host: gpu-node-12 at 2026-03-17T15:02:21Z. Suggested action: increase pinned pool or pre-warm allocations.
Priya: action items?
Jamie: (1) add a diagnostic flag to batcher to log timed-waits and flush triggers, (2) add a metric for pinned pool exhaustion to console, (3) try increasing pinned pool to see if overlap improves.
Marco: also experiment with kernel selection: long FP32 matmul kernels keep the compute engine busy and increase latency variance. Try switching to the FP16/quantized kernel variant on this sequence length and compare.
Sasha: for immediate test: bump pinned pool by 4x on staging, rerun the nsys capture, and capture `perf` on the submitter thread to ensure no sched gaps.
Alex: will run tests this afternoon and attach new trace. If pinned pool fixes overlap we push a quick mitigation in the allocator + a longer-term microbatching tweak to avoid timed-waits for tiny workloads.
Priya: thanks everyone. If you see other traces with similar pattern drop them here. :thumbsup:
Jamie: I'll add a tiny unit test that simulates pinned exhaustion and asserts we don't fall back to blocking copies silently.
Marco: filed infra ticket INFRA-7321 to increase default pinned pool in staging and add monitoring.
Sasha: ping me when traces uploaded, I'll run a kernel selection benchmark to compare execution profiles.
Alex: uploaded updated nsys: https://internal-artifacts/trace/2629-v2.nsys at 2629009034 — closing loop after analysis.
